A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original modality-permutation experiments, model-size comparisons, category analyses, and GPT-5/Gemini case studies, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical analyses and adds quantitative comparisons involving LLaVA-Next, Qwen2.5-VL, and Qwen3-VL.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same four input conditions, modality-shuffling procedure, subgroup analysis, and majority-vote ensemble. The additional evaluated models do not change the proposed diagnostic method.

E1.justification: Demonstrated benchmark coverage matches, including ADE, which already appears in v1 Figure 4. However, v2 removes MMVet from the experimental sourcing list and changes the conclusion's benchmark count from 24 to 23. Neither version reports MMVet results, leaving actual removal versus documentation correction unresolved.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's quantitative Cambrian comparisons, v2 evaluates LLaVA-Next 7B, Qwen2.5-VL 7B, and Qwen3-VL 8B against Cambrian-8B in Figures 4 and B.11. This substantially broadens the evaluated model comparison set.

E3.justification: The new cross-model experiments introduce 7B/8B configurations alongside the retained 8B/13B/34B scaling study. Accuracy, four input conditions, and ensemble construction remain unchanged. No reported split, preprocessing, or sampling revision explains changes to existing scores.

E4.justification: Figures 4 and B.11 newly test whether modality dependence persists across model families on twelve benchmarks. Figures B.8-B.10 also extend size-sensitivity analysis to benchmarks including ChartQA, COCO, MME, Q-Bench, ScienceQA, Omni3D, and MathVista; other panels retain earlier analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The case studies' model-reported confidence scores are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 3 changes Cambrian-8B AI2D text-only accuracy from 25% to 56% and ensemble normal accuracy from 73% to 77%, without explaining the revisions. Section 4.2 also replaces RealWorldQA with V* in the inter-modality-only group. Numerous model-comparison and scaling results are newly reported.

T1.justification: The dependency definitions, selection-variable formulation in Equation 1, and mathematical expressions for the four evaluation conditions are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract extends persistence of modality dependencies from model sizes to sizes and types. The conclusion adds the stronger assertion that no dataset is truly multi-modal. The central contribution of characterizing heterogeneous benchmark dependencies remains.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies that text and image dependency categories overlap. It replaces the AI2D ensemble-versus-individual-model explanation with dependence increasing with scale, adds possible data-curation explanations, and recommends routinely reporting modality-specific and random baselines. Existing multiple-choice and abstention limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 adds a project code-access link absent from v1, and Section 4.2 identifies the added models' base language models. Appendix sourcing information largely remains, although the explicit DocVQA/InfoVQA exclusion explanation is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for LLaVA-Next, both Qwen models, Wang et al. (2020), Gu et al. (2025), and Suhr and Artzi (2019). These extend supporting context while retaining the same positioning relative to Perceptual Score and Shapley-based approaches.

P1.justification: There are local rewrites throughout the introduction, results, and conclusion, an added model-types discussion, and separate appendix sections A and B replacing A.1 and A.2. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain.

P2.justification: New Figures 4 and B.11 add model-comparison displays. Former Figure A.7 is reorganized and expanded into B.8-B.10, removing its duplicated SEED panel. Figure 2 adds the already evaluated ADE axis, and category radar plots receive revised axes and scaling.

improvement.justification: The new cross-model analyses strengthen support beyond the Cambrian family, while code-access information and clearer dependency categories improve usability. The net gain is limited by unexplained score revisions and inconsistencies: v2 gives Cambrian-8B POPE text-only accuracy as 53% in Figure 3 but 50% in Figure 4. Its stronger conclusion that no dataset is truly multi-modal also exceeds the qualification in its results discussion.
